args.message: Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) per FIN-212

args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but FIN-212 requires banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). This caused the nightly build failure in `tests/test_money.py` (`2.665` must round to `2.66`, not `2.67`).

## Change
- Switch `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Testing
- CI passed on branch `fix/rounding-half-even` (run ci-0001, sha 08d3cd5986), including `tests/test_money.py`.

Done. Here's a summary:

**Problem:** `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but `tests/test_money.py` (per FIN-212) requires banker's rounding — e.g. `2.665` must round to `2.66`, not `2.67`.

**What I did:**
1. Created branch `fix/rounding-half-even` from `main`.
2. Changed `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP` (single-line fix) and committed it.
3. Ran CI (run ci-0001) — passed.
4. The PR was rejected because the branch was behind main, so I merged main into the branch and re-ran CI (run ci-0002) — passed.
5. Opened PR [#101](https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101) against `main` with review requested from **alex**.

The PR is now open and awaiting approval from alex before merging into main (per policy, main merges require code-owner approval).

transcript.reasoning_content: Fix: use ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Note the test expects 2.675 -> 2.68 and 2.665 -> 2.66. With ROUND_HALF_EVEN: 2.675 quantize to 0.01: exact Decimal 2.675 -> half way between 2.67 and 2.68; even last digit: 2.68 (8 is even) -> 2.68 ✓. 2.665 -> between 2.66 and 2.67; even is 2.66 ✓. Good.
